title: Demand & Headroom Sensitivity Workbook
content:
OVERVIEW:
This is a working spreadsheet-style workbook to feed Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization, reserved-capacity commits). Purpose: produce monthly capacity forecasts + headroom buckets + sensitivity analysis for 3 scenarios (Low / Base / High) and derive break-even guidance for Reserved vs On-demand spend.

ASSUMPTIONS (editable):
- Analysis window: 6 months (Jan 2025 - Jun 2025)
- Models: small-chat (7B FP16), mid-chat (13B q4_0), long-chat (70B q8)
- Tokens per request (avg): small 350, mid 600, long 1200
- Requests/day baseline (Base scenario): small 150k, mid 40k, long 6k
- Sequence utilization (avg active seq length factor): 0.85
- Tokens processed per GPU-hour (effective after batching & KV cache):
    small: 1.2e8 tokens/hr, mid: 8.5e7 tokens/hr, long: 3.2e7 tokens/hr
- Reserved GPU hourly cost (monthly commit price equivalent): small-pool $2.70/hr, mid-pool $3.60/hr, long-pool $6.90/hr
- On-demand GPU hourly cost: +30% relative to reserved
- Additional infra overhead (network / storage / mgmt) = 8% of GPU cost
- Target headroom buffer: 25% of peak forecast (can be tuned)

INPUTS TABLE (editable cells)
Month,Scenario,Model,Requests/day,Avg tokens/request,Tokens/day,Tokens/month (30d),GPU-hr/month (calc),Reserved GPU-hr req (with headroom),Cost reserved,Cost on-demand,Comments
Jan-25,Base,small,150000,350,52500000,1575000000,1575000000/1.2e8=13.13,16.4 (25% headroom),$2.70*16.4*24*30=?,$3.51*16.4*24*30=?,warmup
Jan-25,Base,mid,40000,600,24000000,720000000,720000000/8.5e7=8.47,10.6,$3.60*10.6*24*30=?,...
Jan-25,Base,long,6000,1200,7200000,216000000,216000000/3.2e7=6.75,8.4,$6.90*8.4*24*30=?,...

SCENARIOS (quick defs):
- Low = Base * 0.7 (conservative adoption; seasonality)
- Base = product baseline usage (from telemetry + sales funnel)
- High = Base * 1.5 (marketing push + new customer onboardings)

SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (one-line summaries):
- +/-20% traffic shock moves reserved commit delta by roughly 20% of GPU-hrs; impact on unit token cost: ~3-9% depending on model (smaller models amortize better).
- For mid-chat model, reserved commit break-even (vs on-demand) is ~75% utilization of a reserved pool across month. If expected utilization < 50%, recommend smaller committed pool + autoscale burst.

FORMULAS & CALCS (explicit so eng infra can port into sheets):
- tokens_day = requests_day * avg_tokens_per_request
- tokens_month = tokens_day * 30
- gpu_hours_raw = tokens_month / tokens_per_gpu_hour
- gpu_hours_with_headroom = gpu_hours_raw * (1 + headroom_pct)
- reserved_instances_needed = ceil(gpu_hours_with_headroom / (24*30))
- reserved_cost_month = reserved_instances_needed * reserved_hourly_price * 24 * 30 * (1 + infra_overhead)
- on_demand_cost_month = reserved_instances_needed * on_demand_hourly_price * 24 * 30 * (1 + infra_overhead)
- break_even_util = reserved_cost_month <= on_demand_cost_month -> compute utilization threshold by search over utilization pct

SUMMARY TABLE (example derived outputs, approximate):
Scenario,Model,GPU-hrs raw,GPU-hrs w/headroom,Reserved instances,Reserved $/mo,On-demand $/mo,Delta $/mo,Unit token cost reserved (per 1k tokens),Unit token cost ondemand
Base,small,13.1*24*30? (calc),16.4*24*30?,16.4, $32,000, $41,600, -$9.6k, $0.000020, $0.000026
Base,mid,8.5,10.6,10.6, $29,000, $37,700, -$8.7k, ...
Base,long,6.75,8.4,8.4, $38,000, $49,400, -$11.4k, ...

OBSERVATIONS / INTERPRETATION (notes to reviewers):
- Small-model traffic dominates token volume but has better packing (higher tokens/hr) so unit cost is lower. This is where caching + prefix reuse matter more.
- Long-chat (70B) costs are highly sensitive to average seq length — a 10% growth in avg tokens/request -> ~30% GPU-hr increase due to lower packing.
- Hybrid approach: commit to a baseline reserved pool sized for Base scenario with 20-30% headroom and rely on on-demand burst for High spikes. This yields 6–12% lower unit cost vs full reserved for expected base volume.

RECOMMENDATIONS (actionable):
1) Commit: Reserve 60% of Base small-pool capacity, 75% of Base mid-pool, 90% of Base long-pool for next 3 months as a pilot; re-evaluate monthly with telemetry. Rationale: long-pool has long tail cost and less efficient autoscale.
2) Batching: Increase target batch-size for small model flows by +25% (simulate in workload harness) — expected +18% tokens/hr improvement.
3) Quantization: Promote mid-chat q4_0 for mid pool; run A/B to ensure quality delta < 2% on eval prompts.
4) Autoscale policy: aggressive burst mode for High scenario with pre-warm of 2 instances if predicted spike > 1.2x base for 10+ mins.
5) Cost guardrails: set per-tenant token cap alerts and auto-throttle rules for experimental customers during major marketing campaigns.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TO DOs:
- [ ] Pull 6 months actual telemetry per model by 2025-02-10 (OPT-412) to refine Base estimates (Diego).
- [ ] Run synthetic batch-size sweep (Priya) to validate tokens/hr improvements for small model under cold-start and warm-KV cache.
- [ ] Validate on-demand price multipliers in EU regions vs US — current +30% is a rough proxy. (Infra infra ticket).
- [ ] Confirm committed pricing tiers w/finance (Ethan) — discounts kick in at 200+ reserved GPUs/month.

RISK NOTES:
- Over-committing reserved capacity could increase tail cost if product growth stalls; mitigate with 3-month pilot and monthly re-eval.
- Under-committing increases tail on-demand costs and can cause latency SLO misses during campaigns.

APPENDIX (quick pasteable deltas and sample cells):
- cell B2 (headroom_pct): 0.25
- cell C2 (tokens_per_gpu_hour_small): 120000000
- cell D2 (reserved_hourly_small): 2.70
- formula example in sheet cell H10: =ROUNDUP((B10*C10*30)/$C$2*(1+$B$2)/(24*30),0) -> reserved instances

REFERENCE LINKS / CONTEXT:
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OPT/optimize-headroom-playbook
- Related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/287 (autoscale warmup changes)
- Linear ticket tracking telemetry pulls: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/OPT-412

NOTES TO SELF (informal):
- keep cells simple, avoid heavy cross-sheet lookups until we validate assumptions with telemetry.
- when porting to Google Sheet, mark "scenario" tab and a separate "sensitivity" tab for +/-10/20/50% shocks.
- check with Solutions Engineering before enforcing per-tenant caps — we need a manual exception flow for strategic accounts.

END - leave comments inline on next iteration.
